annotation.title_clean: Autonomous vehicles (California Assembly Bill 1777, Chaptered 9/27/2024) — amending Vehicle Code Section 38750 and adding Sections 38751–38753
annotation.title_en: Autonomous vehicles (California Assembly Bill 1777, Chaptered 9/27/2024) — amending Vehicle Code Section 38750 and adding Sections 38751–38753
annotation.summary_en: California statute (chaptered Sept 27, 2024) amending the Vehicle Code on autonomous vehicles. It requires emergency response phone lines, two-way communication with remote operators, emergency geofencing compliance within two minutes, and police-issued notices of AV noncompliance. It also keeps DMV permitting, $5M insurance, data recorders, and a zero-emission requirement from 2030.
key_provisions_or_claims: Manufacturers of driverless AVs must run a 24/7 emergency response line answered within 30 seconds by a remote human operator able to immobilize or move the vehicle (from July 1, 2026).
Emergency officials can issue geofencing messages; fleets must leave or avoid the area within two minutes.
Peace officers can issue notices of AV noncompliance; manufacturers must report them to the DMV within 72 hours.
AV operation requires DMV approval, $5M insurance/bond, and a 30-second pre-collision sensor data recorder retained three years.
From 2030, AVs of model year 2031+ under 8,501 lbs must be zero-emission to operate under a deployment permit, subject to federal law.
